summary: Tsutomu Yamaguchi works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Hokkaido University and held posts at the Eastern Institute, attested in 2015 and 2026.

Tsuyoshi Yokoyama specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015–2017) and held an appointment as a special researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, attested in 2017.
Tsyben Zhamtsarano worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as Tibetology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University in 1902 and headed the Mongolian Academy of Sciences.

Tu Weiming is a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at Tunghai, Tokai, and Harvard universities under Mou Zongsan, Chun-i Tang, and Fuguan Xu, and held professorships at Princeton, UC Berkeley, Harvard, and Peking University.

Tubten Chokyi Dorje studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He taught Shenphen Nangwa, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
Tubten Gyeltsen Ozer studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Tubten Nyendrak studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Shenphen Nangwa, and taught Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Tubten Tsondru studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Khenpo Gangshar. He taught Palden Sherab and Ringu Tulku.
Tukaram Krishna Laddu worked in Indology. He studied at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg until 1912 and held a post at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, attested in 1920.
Tulku Hungkar Dorje studied under Penor Rinpoche and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.

Tulku Sherdor works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Vassar College, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, and his teachers included Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Ted Norton, and Jeffrey Hopkins.

Tulku Thondup was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dodrupchen Monastery under Kyala Khenpo, Khenpo Chemchok, and Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and served as a visiting scholar at Harvard University.

Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Samten Gyatso, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Karsé Kongtrul, Dzongsar Khyentse 02, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and founded Tergar Osel Ling Monastery.

Turrell V. Wylie worked in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Washington and under Giuseppe Tucci and Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, later serving as associate professor and professor at the University of Washington.
Tutob Chökyi Wangchuk studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Trulshik Rinpoche.
Tyler Dewar works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Nitartha Institute and with traditional teachers Tashi Wangchuk, Acharya Lama Tenpa Gyaltsen, and Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche.
Tyler G. Neill works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Leipzig University by 2022 and held an academic post there, attested in 2022.

Tzungkuen Wen is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Queensland, taught at Fuyan Buddhist Institute in 2005, and later headed the Counseling and Guidance Center at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.
U Dhammissara works in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts degree at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Sanu Mahatthanadull, attested in 2017.
Ugyen Pelgen is a scholar in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed a master's degree at Aligarh Muslim University and served as a lecturer of history at Sherubtse College.
